newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Lone Star says finds gold near Awak Mas.
newsitem.headline: Lone Star says finds gold near Awak Mas.

text.p: Lone Star Exploration NL said on Tuesday it had discovered gold at the Tarra prospect, three km north of its Awak Mas gold project on the island of Sulawesi in Indonesia, following an intensive drilling programme.
It said the discovery was the first to be made outside the two million ounce Awak Mas gold deposit.

Lone Star said it began drilling two weeks ago to follow up promising results from channel sampling which returned 480 metres of continuous mineralisation at 2.68 grams per tonne (g/t) gold from five metre composite samples.
Five rigs were immediately moved to the area.
The first hole, which was drilled at the southern end of the strike length, returned 20.7 metres at 4.12 g/t from 26 metres and 10.5 metres at 2.1 g/t from 95 metres, Lone Star said.
Subsequent holes returned results that included 30 metres at 1.89 g/t from 124 metres, 42 metres at 2.83 g/t from surface, and 11.2 metres at 2.12 g/t from 16.8 metres.
One hole still in progress returned 64 metres at 1.8 g/t and 21 metres at 2.5 g/t, while another hole still in progress returned 39 metres at 1.42 g/t and 22 metres at 1.54 g/t, it said.
Lone Star said the returns indicated mineralisation over a 400 metre strike length but geochemical anomalies indicated the mineralisation may extend at least one km beyond the area drilled so far.
Lone Star said Tarra was one of five regional targets first announced last month following a rethink of its strategy at Awak Mas in the first half of this year.

"This approach has seen the company re-focus on exploration, appoint a new and more technically focused board, implement a new management structure, and secure an extension of the Awak Mas Contract of Work (COW)," it said.
As part of its systematic review of the geology of the area, Lone Star's exploration team has targeted potential satellite deposits within a 5-6 km radius of the Awak Mas deposit., Lone Star said.
Following the extension of the Awak Mas COW, Lone Star has until October 2000 to bring a mine into production at the remote site on Sulawesi, it said.
Drilling would continue at Tarra to further test the width and along-strike continuity of the mineralisation, it said.
Preliminary laboratory-scale metallurgical testwork showed gold recoveries in excess of 90 percent in a variety of composite rock types with head grades in excess of 1.0 g/t gold, Lone Star added.
